report.summary: Potential false-negative gate failure on Windows due to case-sensitive path rebasing. rebase_declared_path uses Path.relative_to which is case-sensitive, so an absolute path with different casing than the resolved primary_root will not be rebased, leading to 'escaped scope' refusal even when the path is actually within the checkout. Concrete trigger: user provides absolute path like C:\repo\daedalus\src\file but primary_root is stored as C:\Repo\Daedalus. The docstring claims any absolute path under primary_root is rebased, but this case is silently dropped, returning raw path.

risks.trigger: Absolute path with different drive letter case or directory case on case-insensitive filesystem (Windows) where primary_root resolves to a differently-cased path.
risks.effect: Task is incorrectly marked as GATES_FAILED because target_paths comparison fails; a valid write is refused.

risks.trigger: Path relative_to fails due to any reason (symlink loop, access denied resolving primary_root) => raw path returned uncritically, no warning logged.
risks.effect: Error swallowed; user gets unexpected failure with no diagnostics.

todos: Fix rebase_declared_path to normalize case before relative_to comparison, e.g., resolve both paths and compare drive and parts case-insensitively on Windows.
Add warning when rebase fails unexpectedly, to alert operator of path configuration issue.

handoff.suggestion: In rebase_declared_path, after raw = str(raw), if Path(raw).is_absolute(), attempt to resolve() and then check with os.path.commonpath or with case-insensitive match. Alternatively, use os.path.relpath on the os-level to get relative path independent of pathlib case-sensitivity. Note that Python's pathlib on Windows does not perform case-insensitive comparison for relative_to (as of Python 3.11). So the code is fragile.
